entries.group: the OSError fallback of migrate's candidate.file_sha256 (bundle_cli.py:1074-1077). L1075 (the success path) sets report['candidate']['file_sha256'] from the just-written file's bytes and is NOT mutated; L1077 runs only when a.out.read_bytes() raises OSError right after the exclusive _create wrote the file (L1072). Both mutants change only L1077, so they are observable solely inside that defensive I/O-failure branch. No registered kill file, no doc scenario, and no operator misuse reaches it: every reader observes the success path. mutant_view confirms 141 is report['candidate']['']=None (file_sha256 key absent) and 162 is report['']['file_sha256']=None (KeyError, caught by the except at L1081 -> 'refused: ...' exit 2).
entries.grounds: In the `except OSError:` arm, `report['candidate']['file_sha256'] = None` becomes `report['candidate'][''] = None`: under an OSError the candidate's file_sha256 key would be missing (replaced by ''). The success-path assignment at L1075 that every reader observes is unmutated. The None-on-failure fallback is undocumented (the docstring :78-79 and the report's own prose L442-444 describe file_sha256 as 'the sha256 of the file's bytes' / 'when the command wrote the file'); read_bytes() reads raw bytes and cannot fail on encoding, so the branch needs a genuine filesystem failure between _create and read-back. No REFUTED-by-measurement.
